Safety Data Sheets (SDS) are standardized documents that contain information about hazardous substances. Based on my knowledge, they typically include:

1. Identification of the substance and supplier
2. Hazard identification
3. Composition/information on ingredients
4. First-aid measures
5. Fire-fighting measures
6. Accidental release measures
7. Handling and storage
8. Exposure controls/personal protection
9. Physical and chemical properties (including flash point, solubility, explosion limits)
10. Stability and reactivity
11. Toxicological information (including acute toxicity data)
12. Ecological information
13. Disposal considerations
14. Transport information
15. Regulatory information
16. Other information

Looking at the options:
A. Date of authorization of the substance by the national or European authority - This is regulatory information but not typically a specific requirement in SDSs
B. Chemical properties (e.g., substance group, alkalinity) - These would be included under composition/information on ingredients
C. Physical properties (e.g. flash point, solubility, explosion limit) - These are specifically included in Section 9 of SDSs
D. Toxicological properties (e.g. acute toxicity limit) - These are specifically included in Section 11 of SDSs

Both options C and D represent information that is definitely required in Safety Data Sheets.
